Slawkow Krzykawka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Krzykawka, Poland

Not demolished. The Jewish cemetery of Sławków is located within the administrative boundaries of the village of Krzykawka, covering 0.39 hectares; its first burials took place in 1904, and in 1907 the Jewish communities of Sławków and Strzemieszyce formalized the land's purchase. Szulim Zając, the community's first rabbi, was buried here in 1928 beneath an erected ohel. The cemetery survived WWII in relatively good condition; the accompanying closure documentation from 1964 states the last burial took place in 1942, though restoration efforts led by Daniel Landsmann in the 1960s were followed by a further burial as late as 1971. Multiple scholarly studies of the cemetery have since been published, including works by D. Rozmus (1999) and a joint study by M. Cyankiewicz, L. Hońdo, D. Rozmus, M. Rozmus, and W. Starościak (2004). Jewish settlement in Sławków developed from the early 19th century, reaching 610 people (16 percent) by 1921, most of whom were murdered by the Germans at Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1942.
